### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via isObjectSchemaMaskExempt (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **145** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dc4a5c630844f04587e790c21ca807f306239518` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c04c5691ed821c9e0965e32cad5fb34be863f480` — the merge of head `a337d0cc537ea09b8a2bee82f9b80270df735b1e` into base `dc4a5c630844f04587e790c21ca807f306239518`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c04c5691ed821c9e0965e32cad5fb34be863f480 && git checkout c04c5691ed821c9e0965e32cad5fb34be863f480
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin dc4a5c630844f04587e790c21ca807f306239518 a337d0cc537ea09b8a2bee82f9b80270df735b1e && git checkout -B drift-repro dc4a5c630844f04587e790c21ca807f306239518 && git merge --no-ff a337d0cc537ea09b8a2bee82f9b80270df735b1e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dc4a5c630844f04587e790c21ca807f306239518
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs dc4a5c630844f04587e790c21ca807f306239518` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a337d0cc537ea09b8a2bee82f9b80270df735b1e`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #22250 (body; triage 6057391955; claim 6058980283 as edited; os-dev-reports 6061977564 and 6063483631), PR #22308 (body, 11-file list, the net diff from merge-base `58707166f` to the head), ADR-0106 D1/D3/D4/D6/D8 on `main`, `packages/spec/src/api/sortability.zod.ts` on `main` and on the head, the `domain:spec` cross-lane declaration on #6017 (6062064959), and the check-runs on the head. Read-only: no worktree, no build, no test, no gate run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Direction (triage: tighten, never loosen) — right.**
- `item.fields` is unchanged for every class. On the head `isObjectSchemaMaskExempt` reads `isSystem`, then `holdsObjectSchemaMaskExemptCapability` over the same `OBJECT_SCHEMA_MASK_EXEMPT_CAPABILITIES` the `main` predicate read inline: the same exempt classes, the definition still served whole; a member is still projected by step 4 of `createMetaItemAnswer` and by `maskObjectDocument` on the cached arm. Pinned per class in all three new suites.
- `sortability` is narrowed only for a D4-exempt caller whose own field permission withholds a field. `translateMetaEnvelope` derives it from `runtimeDocument` (default: `document`), and `resolveObjectSchemaRuntimeView` returns the served document by reference unless the posture is `passthrough` carrying `runtime` AND the answer is `project` AND something is withheld. For a `project`, `undetermined`, `disabled`, `no-service` or `not-applicable` posture the view is the served document, so every non-exempt class and every deployment posture is byte-unchanged. Right.
- Permission read (`/auth/me/permissions`) and the data route: no file of theirs is in the diff, and the door table on a real boot reads both unchanged for all three classes. Right.
- Other runtime or picker-facing projections served beside the definition on `main`: none. `resolveObjectSortability` is the only `resolveObject*` export in `packages/spec/src/api`; in the non-test sources of `rest` and `runtime`, `sortability` is built only inside `translateMetaEnvelope` (item read, `metaType === 'object'`); the list read and the layered answer call no projection. The dev's "sortability is the only one" holds.

**D4 sick-service invariant — right.** `resolveObjectSchemaMaskPosture` still decides exemption before any service call (resolving the posture asks nothing; the `asked === 0` pin is kept). The `runtime` asker is attached only for a capability-exempt caller when an `ask` exists; it is lazy (invoked only by `resolveObjectSchemaRuntimeView`, and only for a document with a `fields` record), memoised (`settled ??= settle()`, so at most one call per posture), and it never rejects: `await ask()` sits inside `try`, and a throw and a non-array answer both return `undetermined` with one `warn`. The exempt caller's definition read cannot become a 5xx, so ADR-0106 D4's exempt caller "cannot be turned into an error by a sick security service" holds; D6 tier 3 (throw answers 5xx) stays the non-exempt caller's posture, untouched. Cost note: an exempt item read that serves `sortability` now pays one security call it did not pay on `main`; D4's text constrains faults, not latency.

**Caching / D3 — right.**
- Unrestricted exempt caller: `withheld` is empty, so `fingerprint` is `''`, and `foldVisibilityFingerprintIntoEtag(etag, '')` returns `etag` unchanged: the ETag is byte-identical to `main`. Pinned (`"v1"` and its 304) and measured (`39ce56dc` after unbinding the set).
- An exempt caller and a projected caller denied the same field: the definition mask hashes the bare name, the runtime view hashes `@runtime:` plus the name, and `@` occurs in no machine name, so the two validators cannot collide. Pinned (`not.toBe`) and measured (`39ce56dc~3c4b8092` against `39ce56dc~32c59ec2`).
- No stale 304: `maskApplies` is true for a posture carrying `runtime`, so the protocol is not handed `If-None-Match` and the 304 is judged below against the triple-folded value (visibility, runtime view, intake). A sick-service transition in either direction moves the validator (`v` versus `v~fp`), so a client re-fetches rather than revalidating a body of the other state. An `undetermined` definition posture still answers `private, no-store` with no ETag. The uncached arm emits no ETag, and the runtime dispatcher serves no conditional arm. The cached document is never mutated (the view is a shallow copy with a new `fields`).

**`check:system-context-census` — right.** The head's only `isSystem` read in `object-schema-fls.ts` stays inside `isObjectSchemaMaskExempt`, the page's anchor; `holdsObjectSchemaMaskExemptCapability` reads `systemPermissions` only, and `resolveObjectSchemaMaskPosture` reads no `isSystem`. No new elevation read; the predicate exempts the same classes as `main` for the definition read. `Lint & Repo Gates`, the gate's job, is green on the head.

**Public surface** (judged on the `exports` maps: both packages expose `.` to `dist/index.d.ts`; `metadata-core`'s index re-exports `object-schema-fls.js` whole; `rest`'s index names `translateMetaEnvelope` and `MetaItemAnswerSources`).
- `@objectstack/metadata-core`: `resolveObjectSchemaRuntimeView` (new function) — right. `ObjectSchemaRuntimeView` (new interface) — right. `ObjectSchemaRuntimeFieldPosture` (new type) — right. `ObjectSchemaMaskPosture`'s `passthrough` member gains an optional `runtime` (a function answering a promise of the field posture) — additive: a consumer constructing a posture is unaffected; a consumer comparing an exempt posture with `toEqual` now sees a function (the one in-repo pin moved to `toMatchObject`). Right. `RUNTIME_VIEW_FINGERPRINT_QUALIFIER`, `holdsObjectSchemaMaskExemptCapability` and `runtimeFieldPostureAsker` are not exported; `isObjectSchemaMaskExempt` and `OBJECT_SCHEMA_MASK_EXEMPT_CAPABILITIES` are unchanged. Nothing narrowed.
- `@objectstack/rest`: `translateMetaEnvelope` gains an optional fifth parameter with a default — right. `MetaItemAnswerSources.translateEnvelope` gains an optional third parameter — right (an implementer with two parameters stays assignable). `RestServer.translateMetaEnvelope` and `metaItemAnswerSources` are `private`, so their signature changes are not in the published declaration. Nothing narrowed.
- `@objectstack/runtime`: no declaration change (`answerMetaItem` is module-internal). Right.
- Wire: `GET /meta/object/:name` and the dispatcher's `/metadata/object/:name` keep their shape; for a restricted D4-exempt caller the `sortability.fields` map loses the withheld entries (absence already means "no platform sort behind this name") and the cached ETag gains a fold. No query parameter, route, or request accept-set change. `@objectstack/spec`: `ObjectSortabilitySchema`'s shape is unchanged; `.describe()` text only.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/22250-meta-fls-runtime-sortability.md`: `@objectstack/metadata-core` **minor** (new exported symbols plus an optional member) — right. `@objectstack/rest` **minor** (optional parameters on an exported function and an exported interface) — right under the WHICH LEVEL rule (a `fix(` that widens an index is `minor`). `@objectstack/runtime` **patch** (behaviour only; no declaration moved) — right. Pre mode is on (`.changeset/pre.json`, tag `next`), which does not change the grades; the `fixed` group applies the highest bump to every member.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` stands in the PR body and in the changeset body and matches the claim's edited line. Both arms of the entry gate hit (a `packages/spec/src/**` path and a `yes` declaration), which is what this record answers. The `check-changeset-no-major` level axis is satisfied by two `minor` grades; nothing breaking, so no ADR-0087 disposition is owed.
- No `@objectstack/spec` entry. Three published spec artifacts do change content: `src/api/sortability.zod.ts` ships in the tarball (`files`), `dist` carries the new `.describe()` string, and `json-schema/` (gitignored, built at publish) will carry the new description. But no shape, key, enum or accept set moves, so no `minor` is owed and no Clause-② arm arises from spec; the `fixed` group republishes `@objectstack/spec` at the same bump regardless; and no gate requires an entry (`Check Changeset`, `check-empty-changeset` and the level axis are all green). Judged right for the level. Completeness note for the dispatch seat's ACCEPT, since changeset prose is outside this record's face: the changeset body names no spec file, so the compiled release notes will not say the projection's published description was amended; a `"@objectstack/spec": patch` line, or one sentence in the existing body, closes that. Not a FAIL condition.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Round-1 Q1 (claim `no` versus measured `yes`)** — answered by the seat as option A; right. The shared normaliser belongs in `metadata-core` so the two transports cannot drift; two transport-local copies would be the two-implementations shape the skill refuses.
- **Round-1 Q2 (amend the spec text?)** — answered as option A, riding this PR with `packages/spec` lifted for text only and declared cross-lane on #6017 (6062064959, which names the file and "text only"); no objection posted on #22250. Right. The `resolveObjectSortability` docblock amendment the declaration did not name by symbol is inside the declared file and is text only — covered.
- **Spec text, per caller class (security service healthy, mask enabled):** member — the served map already excludes the withheld field and the projection equals `resolveObjectSortability(item)`: true. Platform admin and organization admin (capability-exempt) — served the field in `item`, no entry: true, pinned on both transports and both arms. `isSystem` — `resolveProjectionFieldMask` answers all fields for a system caller, so nothing is withheld and no entry is missing: true. Nothing else the text says changes: cases 1 to 4 keep their verdicts, the absent-name list only gains a member, and `resolveObjectSortability` still judges by the spec's own predicates — it is handed a narrower document, it does not read a caller. Two deployment postures, not caller classes, fall outside the sentence exactly as they fell outside the previous sentence: under the D8 escape hatch the whole metadata plane is unmasked by choice, projection included; under a sick service (D6 tier 2, or the D4 asker settling `undetermined`) the projection is served unprojected with one `warn`. The spec text describes the enforced posture; the degraded ones are stated in `metadata-core`'s docblocks and in the changeset's "Failure posture". Not escalated.
- **Generated docs:** `protocol.mdx`'s table row is the `.describe()` string joined verbatim; `sortability.mdx`'s case 5 and amended case 1 are the docblock's lines verbatim. `check:docs` runs inside the green `TypeScript Type Check` job, which is the mechanical proof neither was hand-edited.
- **Acceptance note 1 (objectui `column-sortability.ts` docblock):** another repository; the sentence is present at the pinned sha `a58626c8`; the consumer contract (absence means no sort) is unchanged, so the objectui code stays correct and only its comment goes stale; a carrier is named. Correctly not this PR's; not made worse.
- **Acceptance note 2 (`maskingRule` fields listed sortable):** pre-existing for every class on `main` (`getQueryableFields` holds a partially masked field readable but not queryable, while `sortability` keys on readability). This PR keys the runtime view on the same `getMetadataReadableFields` the mask uses, so the exempt class now behaves exactly as the member already did. Read from source, and no in-repo app declares a `maskingRule`, so there is no repro to file; Prime Directive #10 puts it in the notes. Correctly not this PR's; not made worse.
- **Acceptance note 3 (ADR-0015 external injected columns re-added by `unprovisionedInjectedColumns`):** pre-existing for every class; for an exempt caller the narrowed view now meets the same re-add path the member's masked document already met. Correctly not this PR's; not made worse. The carrier being "none" is a weakness of the note, not a defect of the diff.
- **Dev deviations:** the door table measured at `8b412a83e2` was re-measured on this head with no differing cell — closed. Ablation B's void and refused attempts are disclosed and only the third reading is cited — accepted. The `pnpm test -- --maxWorkers=2` misspelling ran the whole package — harmless. No labels written. `main` was not re-merged after `9865012548`, on a clean `merge-tree` with zero file overlap — the queue rebuilds on current `main` anyway. Case 5 cites the card number inside a code docblock that renders into the reference page — the repo's bracketed-number code-comment convention; `check:doc-authoring` and `check-issue-citations` are green.
- **Predicate nuance, noted, not escalated:** the `runtime` docblock says "never `isSystem`", but the asker is attached to any context `isObjectSchemaMaskExempt` admits that also holds an exempt capability, `isSystem` included. Every system context in `core`, `runtime`, `rest` and `plugin-auth` carries no `systemPermissions`, and for a system caller the service answers all fields, so such a context would withhold nothing and warn nothing — one extra service call at most.
- **CI (check-runs on the head, latest per name):** `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` all read `success`. Every other check reads `success`; the body-scoped checks (`Check Changeset`, the three claim checks, `Part-of PR must not also close its card`) re-ran after the seat's body write and read `success`; `Auto Label`, `Check PR Size`, `Console Pin Gate` and the opt-in tarball smoke read `skipped`, not red. No red check. The head is on the base repository (no fork), 813 changed lines, and no governed path is in the file list.
